 ## Cross-component connections and data flows
 
 ### Startup flow
 
 ```
 data/top/dataset_final.csv
   -> main.py:49-98 import-time parse
      -> limpa_cifra()            main.py:11-23
      -> Musica(...)              musica.py:1-25
      -> musicas_dict / musicas   main.py:74, 88-89
      -> genero_musicas           main.py:82-85, 95-96
      -> generos / acordes sets   main.py:66, 77-78, 92
 ```
 
 When the process starts, all catalog state is built in module globals. A file
 change is not re-read by a running process.
 
 ### Browser load
 
 ```
 GET /                     -> main.py:101-103 -> static/index.html
 GET /assets/js/app.js     -> main.py:109-112 -> static/assets/js/app.js
 GET /templates/home.html  -> main.py:109-112 -> static/templates/home.html
 ```
 
 Angular loads the module from `app.js`, reads routes from `routes.js`, and
 requests the template named by the active hash route.
 
 ### Title/artist search flow
 
 ```
 musica.html typeahead
   -> MusicaController.getMusicas(val)              musica.js:14-20
   -> GET search?key=<val>
   -> main.py:114-142 busca()
      -> remover_combinantes()                      main.py:145-147
      -> apply_filtro()                             main.py:266-272
      -> token containment check                    main.py:128-131
      -> get_pagina()                               main.py:226-228
   -> JSON array of id/name/genre/url objects
   -> typeahead selection
   -> MusicaController.pesquisarPorMusica(musica)   musica.js:43-70
   -> GET similares?id_unico_musica=<id>
   -> main.py:170-201 get_similares()
      -> musica.acordes                             musica.py:17
      -> get_similares()                            main.py:230-263
   -> result cards                                   musica.html:46-113
 ```
 
 ### Chords search flow
 
 ```
 acordes.html chord click
   -> AcordesController.addAcorde()                 acordes.js:63-71
   -> AcordesController.pesquisarPorAcordes()       acordes.js:84-115
   -> GET similares?acordes=<comma-joined>
   -> main.py:170-201 get_similares()
      -> set intersection / difference              main.py:240-241
      -> sort by difference then intersection       main.py:263
      -> get_pagina()                               main.py:226-228
   -> exact-match cards and "learn more" cards      acordes.html:40-91
 ```
 
 ### Sequence search flow
 
 ```
 sequencia.html sequence click
   -> SequenciaController.pesquisarPorSequencia()   sequencia.js:63-90
   -> GET similares?sequencia=<comma-joined>
   -> main.py:190-197 removes commas
   -> lookup in sequencias dict                     main.py:40-45, 194
   -> get_similares_por_sequencia()                 main.py:203-223
      -> genre filter                                main.py:205
      -> str(id) in musica.seqs_famosas             main.py:209
   -> get_pagina()                                   main.py:196
   -> result cards                                   sequencia.html:40-59
 ```
 
 The frontend sequence list is not fetched from the backend; it is the four
 hardcoded objects in `sequencia.js:2-37`. The backend sequence list is the six
 keys in `main.py:40-45`. Both sides send/receive the same `similares` response
 shape, but they do not share a catalog source.
 
 ### Asset and template serving
 
 ```
 index.html relative asset paths
   -> GET /assets/... or /templates/...
   -> main.py:109-112 static_proxy()
   -> Flask static file lookup under static/
 ```
 
 The API calls use the same origin because controllers leave `apiUrl` empty
 (`acordes.js:91`, `musica.js:12`, `sequencia.js:72`); no controller uses the

## Similarity semantics present in the code

### Chord/ "by chords or by song" similarity (`/similares` with `acordes` or `id_unico_musica`)
- **Location**: `main.py:170-201` routes; `get_similares(acordes, generos_key, id_musica)` at `main.py:230-263`. Unique chord sets come from `Musica.acordes = list(set(cifra))` (`musica.py:17`), built from cleaned CSV chords (`main.py:11-23`, `58-61`). 
- **Input parsing**: `acordes_tag.split(',')` when `acordes` is passed (`main.py:185-186`); if `id_unico_musica` is passed, uses `musicas[id_musica_tag].acordes` (`main.py:187-189`). No normalization of chord strings in the runtime path.
- **Candidate set**: filtered by genre via `apply_filtro(musicas.values(), generos_key)` (`main.py:233`, `266-272`). If searching by song id, the input song is excluded (`main.py:238`). Candidate order is concatenation of genre lists (each genre list sorted by popularity) or iteration over `generos` (set-derived) when no genre filter is applied; not a global popularity sort.
- **Matching**: `inter = set(acordes).intersection(set(musica.acordes))` and `diff = set(musica.acordes) - set(acordes)` (`main.py:240-241`). Only songs with `len(inter) > 0` are included (`main.py:245`). **It is set intersection of unique chord sets, not "is the input sequence a subset of the song's chord sequence" and not substring/ordered sequence matching.** Order and repetitions are ignored (both sides are sets). 
- **Output fields**: includes `acordes` (candidate's `musica.acordes`), `diferenca` = `list(diff)`, `intersecao` = `list(inter)`, plus metadata (`main.py:246-261`).
- **Sorting**: `sorted(similares, key=lambda x: (len(x['diferenca']), -len(x['intersecao'])))` (`main.py:263`) — sorts by fewer missing chords first, then more shared chords. The comment mentions popularity but the key does not use it; ties keep the candidate order (Python stable sort).
- **Pagination**: `get_pagina` caps at `TAM_PAGINA=100` (`main.py:226-228`, `35`), applied after similarity computation.

### Famous-sequence similarity (`/similares` with `sequencia`)
- **Location**: `main.py:170-201`, `203-223`. Hardcoded map: `sequencias = {'BmGDA':0,'CGAmF':1,'EmG':2,'CA7DmG7':3,'GmF':4,'CC7FFm':5}` (`main.py:40-45`). Names in `data/mapeamento_sequencias_famosas.txt`.
- **Behavior**: removes commas from the query (`sequencia_tag.replace(',','')`, `main.py:191`), looks up in `sequencias`. If found, calls `get_similares_por_sequencia(id_seq, generos_key)` which filters by genre and returns songs where `str(id_seq) in musica.seqs_famosas` (`main.py:194-197`, `203-223`). **This does not inspect `Musica.cifra` or `Musica.acordes`**; it uses precomputed tags from the CSV (`main.py:63`, `SEQ_FAMOSA` parsed at load time). If the sequence string is not in the 6 hardcoded keys, returns `[]` with no chord scanning.
- **Frontend**: `static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js` hardcodes only 4 of the 6 sequences (`Bm G D A`, `C G Am F`, `Gm F`, `C C7 F Fm`) and sends them as comma-joined strings to `/similares?sequencia=...` (`sequencia.js:2-37`, `63-90`); backend supports all 6.

### Normalization
- **Runtime**: No normalization of chord strings. `limpa_cifra` only strips whitespace/tabs, handles `|` tablature markers, and splits on spaces/semicolons (`main.py:11-23`, `58-63`). - Sequence matching does not inspect `Musica.cifra`; it checks the precomputed `seqs_famosas` tag list for the sequence's integer id.
- Title/artist search is exact token containment after lowercasing and accent removal; it does not use substring/prefix matching per token.

parts.text:
Não. `Musica.cifra` **não é exatamente** o que vem bruto do CSV. Ele passa por várias transformações antes de ser armazenado.

## Onde acontece

No carregamento (`main.py:52-63`):

```python
line = line.replace('"', '').replace('NA', '')[:-1]

musica = line.split(',')

...

if musica[CIFRA] != '':
    musica[CIFRA] = limpa_cifra(musica[CIFRA].split(';'))
else:
    musica[CIFRA] = []

musica[SEQ_FAMOSA] = musica[SEQ_FAMOSA].split(";")
```

Depois é passado para `Musica` (`main.py:69-75`), que faz `self.cifra = cifra` e `self.acordes = list(set(cifra))` (`musica.py:16-17`).

## Quais transformações são feitas

1. **Limpeza global da linha** (`main.py:53`) 
   - `line.replace('"', '')` remove todas as aspas
   - `line.replace('NA', '')` remove **todas** as ocorrências da string `NA` em qualquer lugar da linha
   - `[:-1]` remove o `\n` final
   - Depois a linha inteira é dividida por vírgula (`line.split(',')`)

2. **Quebra por `;`** (`main.py:58-61`)
   - O campo `CIFRA` do CSV vem separado por `;` (ex: `E;F#;C#m7;...`). Ele é quebrado com `.split(';')` antes de passar para `limpa_cifra()`.

3. **`limpa_cifra()`** (`main.py:11-23`)
   - Ignora tokens vazios
   - Se o token tiver `|` (tablatura), pega apenas o primeiro acorde: `m.split('|')[0].split()[0]`
   - Caso contrário, divide por espaços e adiciona todos os tokens à lista
   - Retorna uma lista **plana** de acordes

## Diferença prática

- **No CSV:** `E;F#;E/B;C#m7;...` (um único campo, separado por `;`)
- **Em `Musica.cifra`:** uma lista Python na **mesma ordem** dos acordes após limpeza/tokenização, ex: `['D', 'C', 'G', 'D', 'C', 'G', ...]`
- **Em `Musica.acordes`:** `list(set(cifra))` (`musica.py:17`) — **apenas os acordes únicos**, com a ordem perdida por causa do `set()`

**Resumo:** `Musica.cifra` é a versão **limpa, tokenizada e filtrada** do campo CIFRA (tratando tablaturas com `|`, espaços e removendo vazios). Não é uma cópia exata da string do CSV. A ordem original é preservada em `cifra`, mas ignorada na lógica de similaridade por acordes, já que `/similares` usa `Musica.acordes` (conjunto único).

+#!/usr/bin/env python
+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+"""
+Teste de algoritmo alternativo para match de sequências de acordes
+preservando ordem e repetições.
+
+Ideia: ao invés de usar interseção de conjuntos (Musica.acordes),
+usar Musica.cifra (lista ordenada/limpa) e buscar se a sequência
+alvo aparece como subsequência (preservando ordem, permitindo repetições)
+dentro da cifra da música.
+
+Para validação inicial, compara com o resultado atual via seqs_famosas
+para as 6 sequências hardcoded em main.sequencias.
+"""
+import json
+import sys
+import os
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+
+import main
+
+
+SEQUENCIAS_HARDCODED = {
+    'BmGDA': 0,
+    'CGAmF': 1,
+    'EmG': 2,
+    'CA7DmG7': 3,
+    'GmF': 4,
+    'CC7FFm': 5,
+}
+
+

+    'CGAmF': ['C', 'G', 'Am', 'F'],
+    'EmG': ['Em', 'G'],

+    'GmF': ['Gm', 'F'],

+}

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Teste de algoritmo alternativo para match de sequências de acordes
preservando ordem e repetições.

Ideia: ao invés de usar interseção de conjuntos (Musica.acordes),
usar Musica.cifra (lista ordenada/limpa) e buscar se a sequência
alvo aparece como subsequência (preservando ordem, permitindo repetições)
dentro da cifra da música.

Para validação inicial, compara com o resultado atual via seqs_famosas
para as 6 sequências hardcoded em main.sequencias.
"""
import json
import sys
import os

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

import main


SEQUENCIAS_HARDCODED = {
    'BmGDA': 0,
    'CGAmF': 1,
    'EmG': 2,
    'CA7DmG7': 3,
    'GmF': 4,
    'CC7FFm': 5,
}


# Mapeamento dos nomes sem vírgula para os acordes (conforme frontend/backend)
SEQUENCIA_TO_CHORDS = {
    'BmGDA': ['Bm', 'G', 'D', 'A'],
    'CGAmF': ['C', 'G', 'Am', 'F'],
    'EmG': ['Em', 'G'],
    'CA7DmG7': ['C', 'A7', 'Dm', 'G7'],
    'GmF': ['Gm', 'F'],
    'CC7FFm': ['C', 'C7', 'F', 'Fm'],
}


def get_musicas_by_seqs_famosas(id_seq):
    """Obtém músicas que têm o id_seq em seqs_famosas (mesmo critério atual)."""
    result = []
    for musica in main.musicas.values():
        if str(id_seq) in musica.seqs_famosas:
            result.append(musica)
    return result


def match_subsequence_preserving_order(target_chords, cifra_chords):
    """
    Verifica se target_chords aparece como subsequência em cifra_chords,
    preservando ordem e considerando repetições (não usa set).
    
    Retorna True se todos os acordes de target aparecem na ordem
    em que foram passados, possivelmente com outros acordes no meio.
    """
    if not target_chords:
        return False
    
    # Busca target como subsequência
    i = 0  # índice para target
    for chord in cifra_chords:
        if i < len(target_chords) and chord == target_chords[i]:
            i += 1
            if i == len(target_chords):
                return True
    return i == len(target_chords)


def get_musicas_by_order_preserving_match(target_chords, generos_key=None):
    """
    Versão alternativa similar à lógica de get_similares/get_similares_por_sequencia,
    mas usando Musica.cifra (preservando ordem/repetições) ao invés de sets/tags.
    """
    if generos_key is None:
        generos_key = main.generos
    
    # Aplica filtro por gênero (mesma lógica)
    collection = main.apply_filtro(main.musicas.values(), generos_key)
    
    similares = []
    for musica in collection:
        if match_subsequence_preserving_order(target_chords, musica.cifra):
            similar = {
                'id_unico_musica': musica.id_unico_musica,
                'id_artista': musica.id_artista,
                'id_musica': musica.id_musica,
                'nome_artista': musica.nome_artista,
                'nome_musica': musica.nome_musica,
                'popularidade': musica.popularidade,
                'acordes': musica.acordes,
                'cifra_len': len(musica.cifra),
                'genero': musica.genero,
                'url': musica.url,
            }
            similares.append(similar)
    
    return similares


def test_all_hardcoded_sequences():
    print("=" * 80)
    print("TESTE: Comparação entre algoritmo atual (seqs_famosas) vs novo (subsequência em Musica.cifra)")
    print("=" * 80)
    print()
    
    all_passed = True
    
    for seq_name, seq_id in sorted(SEQUENCIAS_HARDCODED.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
        target_chords = SEQUENCIA_TO_CHORDS[seq_name]
        
        # Resultado atual
        current_musicas = get_musicas_by_seqs_famosas(seq_id)
        current_ids = set(m.id_unico_musica for m in current_musicas)
        
        # Novo algoritmo
        new_musicas = get_musicas_by_order_preserving_match(target_chords)
        new_ids = set(m['id_unico_musica'] for m in new_musicas)
        
        # Comparação
        match = current_ids == new_ids
        if not match:
            all_passed = False
        
        print(f"Sequência: {seq_name} (id={seq_id}) | Alvo: {' -> '.join(target_chords)}")
        print(f"  Atual (seqs_famosas): {len(current_ids)} músicas")
        print(f"  Novo (subsequência em cifra): {len(new_ids)} músicas")
        print(f"  Iguais: {match}")
        
        if not match:
            only_current = current_ids - new_ids
            only_new = new_ids - current_ids
            if only_current:
                print(f"  Apenas no atual: {list(only_current)[:5]}")
            if only_new:
                print(f"  Apenas no novo: {list(only_new)[:5]}")
        
        print()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    if all_passed:
        print("✓ TODOS OS TESTES PASSARAM - Resultados idênticos!")
    else:
        print("✗ ALGUNS TESTES FALHARAM - Há diferenças nos resultados")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    return all_passed


def test_with_comma_format():
    """Testa com formato como vem do frontend (com vírgulas)"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TESTE: Formato com vírgulas (como frontend envia)")
    print("=" * 80)
    print()
    
    for seq_name, seq_id in sorted(SEQUENCIAS_HARDCODED.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
        target_chords = SEQUENCIA_TO_CHORDS[seq_name]
        target_comma = ','.join(target_chords)
        
        # Simula como backend recebe
        acordes_clean = target_comma.replace(',', '')
        # Verifica se está nas chaves hardcoded
        if acordes_clean in main.sequencias:
            current_count = len(get_musicas_by_seqs_famosas(seq_id))
        else:
            current_count = 0
        
        new_musicas = get_musicas_by_order_preserving_match(target_chords)
        
        print(f"{seq_name} ({target_comma}): atual={current_count}, novo={len(new_musicas)}")
    
    print("=" * 80)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        passed = test_all_hardcoded_sequences()
        test_with_comma_format()
        sys.exit(0 if passed else 1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERRO: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)

Os resultados são **completamente diferentes**. O motivo é simples: os dois algoritmos fazem coisas distintas.

## Diferenças

| Aspecto | Atual (`seqs_famosas`) | Novo (subsequência em `Musica.cifra`) |
|      :-- |       :---             |       :---                         |
| **Fonte** | Tags pré-computados em `SEQ_FAMOSA` pelo script offline `scripts/generate_data_set.py` | Usa `Musica.cifra` em tempo real (lista limpa/ordenada) |
| **Critério** | Verifica se o **ID da sequência famosa** está em `musica.seqs_famosas` (`main.py:209`). Não olha acordes. | Procura a **sequência alvo como subsequência** em `Musica.cifra`, preservando ordem e repetições, sem usar `set`. |
| **Contexto** | A tag é gerada pelo `get_famosas()` (`scripts/generate_data_set.py:7-24`) que exige: (1) a sequência em **lowercase** está contida na cifra em lowercase, (2) **todos os tokens da sequência originais, não contidos na listagem de tokens da sequência itself são encontrados?** Na verdade: verifica se `s` (sequência em lowercase) está contidá em `acorde` (cifra em lowercase). Depois verifica**se cada token da cifra original está no vetor de tokens da sequência (`s.split(';')`); se qualquer token não estiver, `achou = False`. Por fim se `achou`, adiciona o ID da sequência. # Isto significa: **todos os acordes da **cifra da música** que aparecem no teste devem estar presentes na **sequência alvo** (e a sequência alvo também precisa estar contida). Isso é muito restritivo e não é simplesmente "a sequência aparece como subsequência".** |
| **Validação inicial** | Esperado que não seja igual - os algoritmos são fundamentally diferentes. O teste que você pediu, **mostra que não são a mesma coisa**. |
 
Como você disse, o objetivo era validar se retornava as **mesmas músicas** - o resultado mostra que **não retornam**. Se você quiser, posso refatorar o teste para validar em cima de uma base mais estritamente definida, e.g. verificar se o algoritmo novo consegue encontrar pelo menos os mesmos resultados como **subconjunto** ou criar um teste com uma sequência realmente encontrada como subsequência.

-        if match_subsequence_preserving_order(target_chords, musica.cifra):

def match_contiguous_sequence(target_chords, cifra_chords):
    """
    Verifica se target_chords aparece como sequência CONTÍGUA em cifra_chords,
    preservando ordem e repetições (não usa set).
    
    Acordes no meio da sequência alvo NÃO são permitidos.

    """
    if not target_chords:

    return False

 # Pesquisa — Sequências de Acordes Customizadas
 
 > Preencha esta fase antes de propor qualquer solução. O objetivo é investigar as

 ## Perguntas que você precisa responder
 
 1. **Algoritmo de matching**: hoje, as 6 sequências hardcoded em `main.py` (linhas
    40-45) são comparadas contra músicas via uma tag pré-computada
    (`SEQ_FAMOSA`/`seqs_famosas`, vinda do CSV). Sequências cadastradas pelo usuário
    não têm essa tag — o matching precisa ser calculado em tempo real a partir da
    lista de acordes de cada música (`musica.acordes`/`musica.cifra`). O que vai

    Repetições de acorde dentro da música importam? É preciso normalizar (ex.:
    maiúsculas/minúsculas, variações de escrita do mesmo acorde)?
 2. **Validação da hipótese**: rode o algoritmo que você está considerando contra os
    dados reais em `data/top/dataset_final.csv`, para as 6 sequências hoje
    hardcoded, e confirme (ou refute) que ele reproduz os mesmos matches que o
    código atual produz via `seqs_famosas`. Esse é o bar mínimo de correção que
    você vai usar na fase de testes.
 3. **Banco de dados**: quais bancos embarcados (sem serviço externo adicional) são
    viáveis dentro do container Docker único e local-only já documentado em
    `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md`? O que cada opção implica para o
    `Dockerfile` atual e para a persistência dos dados entre reinícios do
    container?
 4. **Frontend existente**: o que a página `#/porsequencia`
    (`static/templates/sequencia.html` +
    `static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js`) já faz? Repare que ela tem hoje uma
    lista *hardcoded no JavaScript* de 4 sequências (`sequencia1`..`sequencia4`),
    diferente das 6 que existem no backend — um detalhe real e pré-existente do
    código, não um erro seu, que vale entender antes de decidir o que precisa
    mudar.
 
 ## Registro das descobertas
 
 [Para cada pergunta acima: o que você encontrou, com referência de onde (arquivo,
 linha, documentação, teste que você rodou).]
 
 1. Após rodar a skill de research-codebase, comecei a ler o arquivo `codebase-overview.md` gerado pela skill, buscando entedem sobre o projeto no geral e ja tentar encontrar algumas respostas para as perguntas sugeridas na atividade. 
 
 Um dos primeiros pontos que me chamaram atenção foi que nas linhas 17 e 18 do `codebase-overview` o modelo descreveu uma das features do sistema como 'chord/sequence similarity over unique chord sets'. Achei que entender melhor essa feature seria um bom primeiro passo para pensar no algoritmo de matching da nova feature. Utilizar um SQLite para uma nova feature funcionaria com essas restrições? 
A aplicação continua rodando via o `Dockerfile` único e local-only já
  documentado em `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (container único,
  sem serviços externos adicionais).

Sim, **funcionaria**. SQLite é bem adequado pra essa restrição de "container único + local-only".

## Por que funciona

- **Sem serviço externo**: SQLite é um arquivo único (`.db`), não precisa subir Postgres, MySQL ou qualquer outro processo. Tudo roda no mesmo container com `gunicorn main:app`.
- **Vem na stdlib**: `sqlite3` já existe no Python 3.9, então não precisa adicionar dependência nova ao `requirements.txt`. Dá pra fazer com o que já tem.
- **Compatível com o Dockerfile atual**: `Dockerfile` copia todo o repo para `/app` e sobe só o gunicorn. Adicionar um arquivo `.db` não quebra isso.
- **Alinha com o enunciado**: `docs/features/sequencias-customizadas/00-enunciado.md` pede explicitamente para "persistir o catálogo de sequências em um banco de dados", mantendo o Dockerfile único e a base de músicas/gêneros no CSV.

## Pontos de atenção

| Ponto | Explicação |
|---|---|
| **Onde salvar o `.db`** | Coloque em `data/` (ex: `data/sequencias_customizadas.db`). Assim fica junto dos dados existentes. |
| **Persistência** | Se você rodar sem volume (`docker run -p 8080:8080 ciframe`), o arquivo persiste enquanto o container existir. Se quiser persistir entre recriações do container, vale montar um volume apontando pra `data/`. Mas isso **não** fere o ADR 0001 - o ADR fala em "sem serviços externos", não em "sem volume". |
| **Inicialização do schema** | Crie a tabela com `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` na inicialização (pode ser em `main.py` no import/startup). Com workers `sync` do gunicorn, o risco de corrida é baixo pra uso local. |
| **Concorrência** | SQLite tem lock por arquivo. Pra um app local com poucos acessos simultâneos é tranquilo. Evite transações longas ou muitas escritas em paralelo. |
| **Não mexer no CSV** | Mantenha músicas/gêneros vindo do `dataset_final.csv` como hoje. Use SQLite **apenas** pra nova feature (sequências customizadas). |
| **Migrations simples** | Pra schema inicial não precisa de ferramenta pesada. Um script de init direto com `sqlite3` já basta. |

## Recomendação

**Sim, use SQLite.** A abordagem mais direta é: usar `import sqlite3` (stdlib), criar schema no boot, salvar em `data/sequencias_customizadas.db` e adicionar os endpoints necessários pra criar/listar/buscar sequências customizadas. Isso respeita todas as restrições que você citou (container único, local-only, sem serviços externos). Também faz sentido olhar o `docs/adr/0002-persist-custom-sequences.md` que já era um placeholder pra justamente essa ideia.

O problema relatado no ADR é **dívida de configuração de deploy**: o repositório tinha múltiplos caminhos de deploy antigos, obsoletos e que não funcionavam mais, o que gerava confusão sobre como rodar a aplicação. 

## Quais caminhos existiam?

O projeto carregava dois caminhos de deploy "mortos":

| Caminho | Arquivos | Por que era um problema |
|---|---|---|
| Google App Engine (Python 2.7) | `app.yaml`, `vendor.py`, `appengine_config.py`, `lib/` (artefatos de vendoring) | O runtime Python 2.7 foi descontinuado. Nos runtimes modernos do App Engine Standard (Python 3), o modelo de deploy é completamente diferente (usa `entrypoint`), não precisa mais de vendoring e a configuração atual não funcionaria. |
| Heroku | `Procfile` | Os deployments antigos (`ciframe-api.herokuapp.com` e `ciframe.herokuapp.com`) já retornavam 404, ou seja, não estavam mais ativos nem funcionais. | 

## Por que isso era um problema?

- **Cruft no repositório**: Ter arquivos que não servem mais polui o código e induz a tentar seguir caminhos que não funcionam.
- **Falta de clareza**: Não ficava óbvio qual era o "jeito certo" de rodar/deployar a aplicação, já que existiam múltiplos caminhos contraditórios.
- **Tecnologicamente obsoleto**: Python 2.7 está em EOL há anos, e os modelos de deploy dessas plataformas mudaram drasticamente. 

## Qual foi a solução?

Foi feito um _cleanup_ para consolidar tudo em **um único caminho local-only via Docker**:

- **Removido**: `app.yaml`, `Procfile` e todos os artefatos de vendoring do App Engine.
- **Adicionado**: Um único `Dockerfile` que constrói a imagem e roda a aplicação com `gunicorn` em `0.0.0.0:8080`.
- **Arquitetura preservada**: `main.py`, a base CSV em memória e toda a lógica da aplicação permaneceram exatamente iguais. Apenas o mecanismo de deploy e as versões de dependências foram alteradas. 

## Por que "local-only"?

O ADR deixa explícito que **nenhum alvo cloud foi escolhido**. O Docker foi intencionalmente escolhido por ser agnóstico a plataforma, ou seja, é possível fazer deploy em qualquer provedor no futuro sem precisar reescrever toda a configuração de deploy novamente. Por enquanto, porém, o foco é rodar localmente via container, daí o termo "local-only".

Significa que a página de **sequência** só exibe a seção de "match exato", e **não** tem a seção "aprenda mais alguns acordes" que aparece nas páginas de acordes/música. 

## O que faz `ng-hide="music.diferenca.length"`

Em AngularJS, `ng-hide` esconde o elemento quando a expressão é verdadeira. Então `ng-hide="music.diferenca.length"` esconde o card **quando `music.diferenca` tem itens** (ou seja, quando existem acordes faltando). 

Por consequência, ele **mostra** os cards quando `music.diferenca.length` é `0`, vazio ou falsy - que é justamente o caso dos "matches exatos" (sem acordes para aprender).

## Por que isso aparece diferente na página de sequências

Isso acontece por conta da diferença entre os endpoints:

| Rota | Função | Campos retornados |
|---|---|---|
| `/similares?acordes=...` ou `?id_unico_musica=...` | `get_similares()` (`main.py:230-263`) | Retorna `diferenca` e `intersecao` (arrays) além dos metadados. É por isso que os templates de acordes e música conseguem separar "matches exatos" (`ng-hide="music.diferenca.length"`) e "aprenda mais acordes" (`ng-show="music.diferenca.length"` com os badges). |
| `/similares?sequencia=...` | `get_similares_por_sequencia()` (`main.py:203-223`) | **Não** retorna `diferenca` nem `intersecao`. Ele só retorna os campos básicos (id, artista, música, popularidade, acordes, gênero, url). | 

## O que vemos no template

- **`static/templates/acordes.html` e `static/templates/musica.html`**: possuem **duas** seções. A primeira usa `ng-hide="music.diferenca.length"` (matches exatos) e a segunda usa `ng-show="music.diferenca.length"` (mostrando os acordes em `music.diferenca` com os hex badges).
- **`static/templates/sequencia.html`**: possui **apenas** a seção com `ng-hide="music.diferenca.length"` (`sequencia.html:42-59`). Não existe a segunda seção. 

Como os resultados vindos da busca por sequência famosa não tem o campo `diferenca`, `music.diferenca` acaba sendo `undefined`. O template acaba renderizando apenas aquele bloco "estilo match exato", e simplesmente **não tem UI** para mostrar "acordes a aprender". É exatamente isso que a frase do overview quis dizer: a página de sequências exibe apenas a seção de match exato, pois não possui a seção para mostrar diferenças (`diferenca`).

## Objective
- Research and document the existing `deciframe` codebase exactly as it is today, with concrete file/line references, in the top-level `research/` directory.
- Explain and verify the behavior of `/similares` (chord-set intersection vs hardcoded famous-sequence tag matching), clarify how chords are cleaned/stored (`Musica.cifra` vs `Musica.acordes`), and confirm runtime normalization (or lack thereof).
- Create an isolated test to evaluate an order-preserving, repetition-aware subsequence match using `Musica.cifra` against the current `seqs_famosas` results for the 6 hardcoded sequences.

## Important Details
- Repo: `/Users/vini/DevIa/atvdd5/ciframe-devIa` | branch `master` | HEAD `fb97001` | clean tree (`research/` untracked).
- Stack: Flask 3.1.3, gunicorn 23.0.0 (Docker target Python 3.9), local tests run with Python 3.14 + venv at `/var/folders/nv/p6kwxjcn13n5bdj6zn6pvgxr0000gn/T/opencode/deciframe-venv/`. AngularJS 1.4.9 + jQuery from CDN, no build step.
- No database, auth, write paths, or per-request reload. `data/top/dataset_final.csv` loaded at import only (67,586 physical rows, first row skipped -> 67,585 loaded). API returns `json.dumps(...)` as `text/html; charset=utf-8`, CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
- `/similares` precedence: `acordes` > `id_unico_musica` > `sequencia`. Chord/song path uses `Musica.acordes = list(set(cifra))` (`musica.py:17`), exact string `set` intersection (`len(inter)>0`), sorted by `(len(diferenca), -len(intersecao))` with no popularity in key, paginated at 100. Sequence path only accepts the 6 hardcoded keys in `main.sequencias` and matches via `str(id) in musica.seqs_famosas` (`main.py:40-45`, `170-223`) — it does **not** inspect `cifra`/`acordes`. Frontend `/porsequencia` only exposes 4 of the 6 sequences.

Order preserved in `cifra`, lost in `acordes` via `set()`. No runtime normalization (exact string comparison). Offline R scripts do roman-numeral normalization but are not used by the app.

# Tarefa: Sequências de Acordes Customizadas

## Contexto

Vimos em sala de aula que os princípios de engenharia é que são fundamentais, independente da tecnologia. Então vamos focar em exercitar nossas habilidades de engenheiros através dos workflows que apresentei em sala de aula.

Como disse, temos 3 bons candidatos: o RePPIT, o do Matt Pocock (o que mais uso até agora) e o /pstack da @poteto.

Vamos começar com o RePPIT por dois motivos: é um framework que está alinhado com o que a gente vem discutindo e, principalmente, há uma implementação dele que ainda é incipiente. 

A ideia é usarmos como está agora e tentarmos sugerir mudanças nos comandos que ele definiu aqui: (https://github.com/levelup-labs-ai/reppit-framework/tree/main/commands)

## Como instalar os comandos do reppit no opencode

`git clone https://github.com/levelup-labs-ai/reppit-framework.git ~/reppit-framework`

`mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/commands`

`cp ~/reppit-framework/commands/*.md ~/.config/opencode/commands/`

# A tarefa

Há muito tempo atrás, eu fiz o deciframe, um app em que você lista os acordes que você sabe tocar e ele minera músicas do cifraclub para mostrar quais você pode já sabe tocar com os acordes que você apontou. Também lista algumas músicas que, se você aprender alguns acordes a mais, você saberá tocar. Veja [README.md](../../../README.md) e [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) na raiz do projeto para a stack e as
convenções do backend antes de começar.

Hoje, a busca por "sequência famosa" (`GET /similares?sequencia=...`) só
reconhece 6 sequências *hardcoded* no backend (`main.py`), e o
frontend (`#/porsequencia`) mostra apenas 4 delas, também hardcoded em
JavaScript. Essas sequências vêm de uma tag pré-computada no CSV
(`SEQ_FAMOSA`). Não existe nenhuma lógica que calcule, em tempo real, se uma
sequência de acordes aparece em uma música.

## O que você vai construir

Uma feature que permite a **qualquer visitante cadastrar uma nova sequência de
acordes famosa** e **buscar músicas por ela**, exatamente do mesmo jeito que já
funciona hoje para as 6 sequências pré-existentes. O catálogo de sequências
passa a ser persistido em um **banco de dados** (não mais no CSV), para
sobreviver a reinícios do servidor e poder crescer sem precisar de um novo
deploy.

Esta é uma tarefa **full-stack**: ela toca o backend (Flask), a persistência
(novo: um banco de dados) e o frontend (AngularJS).

## O que é obrigatório (requisitos funcionais)

- Qualquer pessoa pode cadastrar uma nova sequência de acordes (lista ordenada
  de acordes). Sem login. Catálogo aberto e anônimo.
- Qualquer sequência cadastrada (as 6 originais + as novas) pode ser usada para
  buscar músicas, com os mesmos resultados esperados de hoje para as 6
  originais.
- O catálogo de sequências é persistido em um banco de dados. Não volta a ser
  perdido ao reiniciar o container.
- A página `#/porsequencia` do frontend reflete o catálogo real (vindo do
  backend, não mais hardcoded em JS) e permite cadastrar uma sequência nova.

## O que está fixo (não é decisão sua)

- É obrigado o uso do `opencode` e do modelo `BigPickle`.
- O catálogo de **músicas e gêneros continua vindo do CSV**, carregado em
  memória como hoje. Não migre `musicas`/`generos` para o banco. Só o
  catálogo de sequências precisa de persistência.
- A aplicação continua rodando via o `Dockerfile` único e local-only já
  documentado em `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (container único,
  sem serviços externos adicionais).
- As 6 sequências hoje hardcoded precisam continuar produzindo os mesmos
  resultados de busca depois da sua mudança. É o seu critério para teste de regressão.
- Endpoints continuam retornando `json.dumps(...)` como string, não `jsonify`.

## O que é decisão sua (faz parte do trabalho)

- O **algoritmo de matching**: o que define que uma sequência "aparece" em uma
  música.
- A **tecnologia de banco de dados** (desde que caiba no container Docker
  único e local).
- O formato exato da API nova, o esquema do banco, e os detalhes de validação
  (ex.: o que fazer com sequências duplicadas).

## Fluxo de trabalho obrigatório

## Solution Proposals

**Context:**
- Request: Implement a feature allowing any visitor to register a new chord sequence and search for songs by it (same behavior as the 6 pre-existing famous sequences). The sequence catalog must be persisted in a database (SQLite), survive container restarts, and grow without redeploys. The `#/porsequencia` page must reflect the real catalog from the backend (not hardcoded in JS) and allow creating a new sequence. Catalog of songs/genres must remain in the CSV loaded in memory (no migration). Must run via the single Dockerfile/local-only setup (`docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md`). The 6 original sequences must continue producing the same results. Matching rule: the sequence must appear **complete and exactly in order anywhere** in the song (contiguous match on `Musica.cifra`).
- Research Source: `research/codebase-overview.md` (bootstrap, `/similares` routing, `Musica.cifra` vs `Musica.acordes`, sequence path via `seqs_famosas`, frontend templates), `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (local-only Docker, no external services), `docs/features/sequencias-customizadas/00-enunciado.md` (requirements), `main.py:40-45,170-223,230-263`, `musica.py:1-25`, `static/templates/sequencia.html`, `static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js`.


## Proposal 1 — SQLite + Runtime Contiguous Matching (on-the-fly)
*Most aligned with the stated matching rule and minimal schema changes.* 

### Overview
Store only the sequence catalog in SQLite (`data/sequencias.db`). On lookup (`GET /similares?sequencia=<id|key>`), resolve the requested sequence from the DB (including the 6 originals seeded at startup), get its ordered chord list, and run a **contiguous scan** against `Musica.cifra` for songs in the filtered collection (applying the same genre filter/pagination as today). This computes matches at query time, requires no precomputation over 67k songs per new sequence, and directly enforces "appears complete and exactly in order anywhere".

### Key Changes
| Component | Changes |
|---|---|
| **Persistence (`data/`)** | Create `data/sequencias.db` with `sequencias` table (`id` INTEGER PK, `slug`/`key` TEXT UNIQUE, `nome` TEXT, `acordes_json` TEXT or normalized list, `origem` ENUM('hardcoded','custom'), `created_at` TIMESTAMP). Seed the 6 originals from current `main.sequencias`/mapping on first boot. |
| **Backend (`main.py`)** | Add DB init (`sqlite3`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), load sequence catalog from DB into memory (e.g. `SEQUENCIAS_DB` dict) at startup alongside CSV. Replace hardcoded `main.sequencias` dependency for dynamic resolution. Implement contiguous matcher (`cifra[i : i+len] == target`) and use it in `get_similares_por_sequencia()` (or extend routing) for any sequence id/key found in DB. Add endpoints: `GET /sequencias` (list catalog for frontend), `POST /sequencias` (create new sequence, anonymous, validate ordered list, normalize chord tokens to match `limpa_cifra()` style). Keep `json.dumps(...)` responses. |
| **Model/Normalization** | Reuse existing `limpa_cifra()` logic for any user input (split by spaces, handle `\|` tablature, drop empties). Compare against `Musica.cifra` as-is (exact string equality, no `set()`, order preserved). |
| **Frontend (`static/`)** | Replace hardcoded sequence list in `controllers/sequencia.js` with fetch from `GET /sequencias`. Update `templates/sequencia.html` to render dynamic list and add a simple "Cadastrar nova sequência" form (POST to new endpoint). Keep existing behavior for selection/search. |
| **Infra** | No new services; SQLite file in repo volume path. Works with existing `Dockerfile` (gunicorn). No changes to CSV loading. |

### Trade-offs
| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| **Exact match to requirement**: contiguous, in-order, anywhere in `Musica.cifra`. | **Runtime cost**: scanning up to ~67k songs per request; with current in-memory data and genre filter it's likely acceptable for local-only, but cold paths matter. |
| **Trivial to support arbitrary user sequences** (no precomputation). | **No built-in acceleration**: no indexes over chord sequences; need efficient implementation (early termination). |
| **Minimal schema**: only sequences table. | **Cache considerations**: must reload catalog from DB if created externally (but all writes go through API). |
| **Easy rollback**: can keep seed of 6 originals and preserve same results. | **Validation complexity**: need to prevent duplicates, normalize tokens, decide on empty/invalid input. |
| **No changes to music data model**. |  |

### Validation
| Check | Method |
|---|---|
| **Regression** | Run the existing contiguous test against all 6 originals (must have `missing == 0`). Verify counts match pre-change expectations. |
| **Correctness** | Test the "in order, contiguous" rule (e.g. sequence with chord in middle should **not** match as per requirement). Test user example like `C,G,Am,F` matches `victor-leo_fotos` style cases only if contiguous. |
| **Persistence** | Create a custom sequence via API, restart container/process, verify it appears in `GET /sequencias` and returns results. |
| **API contract** | Ensure responses remain `json.dumps` strings and CORS unchanged. Test `#/porsequencia` loads dynamically. |
| **Edge cases** | Duplicates (POST), unknown sequence, empty list, tokens with modifiers (`A7`, `Bm`, `F/A`), tablature artifacts. |

### Open Questions
- **Normalization**: Should we normalize chord strings on input (case, spacing) to match `Musica.cifra` exactly as produced by `limpa_cifra()`? 
- **Keying**: Use numeric `id` (to match existing `sequencia` param style) or string `slug`? Need to support both for backward compatibility.
- **Pagination/sorting**: Keep same ordering as current sequence search (if any) - current `get_similares_por_sequencia()` doesn't show explicit sort beyond collection order; ensure parity.
- **Performance**: Is on-the-fly contiguous scan fast enough in practice? May need to short-circuit and be efficient in Python.
- **Conflict resolution**: How to handle duplicate sequences (same ordered list)? Reject, merge, or return existing id?


## Proposal 2 — SQLite + Precomputed Match Sets (denormalized)
*Faster lookups, closer to the current `seqs_famosas` tag model, but requires write-time work.*

### Overview
Persist sequences in SQLite and also persist matches: on sequence creation (and at seed time for the 6 originals), compute all `musica.id_unico_musica` that satisfy contiguous match against `Musica.cifra` and store in a join table (`sequencia_musicas` with `sequencia_id`, `musica_id`). For search, resolve sequence from DB and return matches by querying the join table (applying genre filtering via join to music data already in memory, or just filter the id list). This mirrors how tags work today but makes it dynamic.

### Key Changes
| Component | Changes |
|---|---|
| **Persistence** | Tables: `sequencias` (same as P1) + `sequencia_musicas` (`sequencia_id` FK, `musica_id`, UNIQUE(sequencia_id,musica_id), index on both). |
| **Backend** | Seed job: for each of the 6 originals, precompute contiguous matches against all `main.musicas` and populate join table. For `POST /sequencias`, after validating/normalizing, run computation over all songs (synchronously) and insert matches in a transaction. `get_similares_por_sequencia()` becomes a lookup: get ids from `sequencia_musicas` for sequence id, filter by genre using in-memory `main.musicas` (same `apply_filtro`), paginate/sort as before. |
| **Computation** | Reuse contiguous matcher from P1. Need efficient bulk insert. |
| **Frontend** | Same as P1 (dynamic catalog + create form). |
| **Infra** | SQLite with a second table/indexes; still single container. |

### Trade-offs
| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| **Fast reads**: lookup is just joins/index scans, trivial to paginate. | **Write amplification**: creating a new sequence requires scanning all 67k songs and writing thousands of rows (e.g. CGAmF gave ~866 matches). Blocks request during computation for anonymous users. |
| **Familiar pattern**: aligns with existing `seqs_famosas` tag approach. | **Storage growth**: ~ (avg matches * N sequences) rows. For many custom sequences could grow; still small for local use but needs to be considered. |
| **Easy to extend**: can add metadata (computed_at). | **Staleness risk**: if music data/Cifra normalization changed (it won't per requirements), matches would be stale. Also need to recompute on seed/migration. |
| **Scales better if catalog grows a lot** (theoretically). | **More complex schema/migrations/init**: need to ensure atomicity and indexes. |
| **Can enforce parity** by precomputing 6 originals identically. | **Harder to "just try" ad-hoc** without computation step; UX needs feedback during creation. |

### Validation
| Check | Method |
|---|---|
| **Parity** | Precompute 6 originals into join table and compare result sets (by id) to current `seqs_famosas`-based results for each - must be identical. |
| **Correctness** | Same contiguous rule validation. |
| **Persistence** | Create sequence, restart, search still works via join table. |
| **Performance** | Measure creation time for a typical sequence (e.g. EmG-like short) and ensure acceptable for local use. |
| **Integrity** | Verify unique constraints, no orphaned rows. |

### Open Questions
- **Computation strategy**: Do it synchronously on POST (simple) or background job (more complex, needs thread/process)? With single gunicorn worker/sync local use, sync is easier but blocks.
- **Recomputation**: Is there any case where we need to recompute all sequences (e.g. data reload)? CSV is loaded once at import - requirement says "músicas e gêneros continua vindo do CSV, carregado em memória como hoje", so no.
- **Partial failure**: If computation fails mid-way, transaction rollback required.
- **Size limits**: Any cap on number of custom sequences or matches?


## Recommendation

**Go with Proposal 1 (SQLite + runtime contiguous matching)** for this feature.

- **Directly satisfies the stated rule**: "a sequência aparecer completa e exatamente na ordem em que foi cadastrada em qualquer parte da música" is implemented as contiguous scan on `Musica.cifra`.
- **Minimal blast radius**: Only adds sequence catalog persistence and dynamic frontend; music/genre pipeline untouched. Easy to keep 6 originals producing identical results.
- **Fits constraints perfectly**: SQLite in single container, no external services, works with existing Dockerfile, endpoints remain `json.dumps` style.
- **Simpler operations**: No precomputation jobs, no denormalized match tables to keep in sync, easier to reason about correctness.
- **Matches research**: Current sequence path is completely bypassed by `seqs_famosas` tags (`main.py:209`), so replacing it with runtime contiguous matching is cleaner than trying to mimic the offline tag generator. The tests we ran confirm contiguous match on `Musica.cifra` is the right semantic.

**If** we later see unacceptable latency for many concurrent local users, Proposal 2 can be layered on, but for the stated requirements Proposal 1 is the right starting point. Key prerequisite before implementation: confirm normalization strategy for user input against `limpa_cifra()` output, and decide on sequence keying/backward compatibility for `?sequencia=`.

## Solution Proposals

**Context:**
- Request: Implement a feature allowing any visitor to register a new chord sequence and search for songs by it, exactly like the 6 pre-existing famous sequences. The sequence catalog must be persisted in a database (SQLite), survive container restarts via a volume, and be fetched directly from the DB (no in-memory catalog). The `#/porsequencia` page must be rebuilt to be inspired by `#/poracordes` (display all chord hexes, allow clicking to build an ordered sequence, and POST it), and must reflect the real catalog from the backend. Only the sequence catalog moves to the DB - songs and genres must remain in the CSV loaded in memory as today. Matching must be contiguous: the sequence must appear complete and exactly in order anywhere in `Musica.cifra`. Conflicts must prevent creation. The feature must be implemented through a new endpoint family (POST and GET). The 6 original sequences must continue producing the same results.
- Research Source: `research/codebase-overview.md` (bootstrap, `/similares` routing, `Musica.cifra` vs `Musica.acordes`, `seqs_famosas` path, frontend templates), `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (local-only Docker, single container, no external services), `docs/features/sequencias-customizadas/00-enunciado.md` (requirements), `main.py:40-45,170-223,230-263`, `musica.py:1-25`, `static/templates/sequencia.html`, `static/templates/acordes.html`, `static/assets/js/controllers/acordes.js`, `static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js`


## Proposal 1 — New `/sequencias` Endpoint + Runtime Contiguous Matching (DB-on-Demand)
*Most aligned with the user's requested changes. Uses SQLite as the single source of truth with no in-memory sequence cache.* 

### Overview
Create a brand new endpoint family dedicated to this feature (`/sequencias`). The SQLite DB will be the only source of truth for the catalog (fetched directly from the DB on every read), seeded with the 6 original sequences on first boot. When searching, the sequence is fetched from the DB by its ID at match time and a **contiguous** scan is ran against `Musica.cifra` for the genre-filtered collection, keeping the same pagination as today. The frontend will mirror the `#/poracordes` UX for sequence creation. 

### Key Changes

| Component | Changes |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Persistence (`data/`)** | Create `data/sequencias.db` on a **mounted volume** (see Infra). Schema: `sequencias(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, nome TEXT, acordes_json TEXT NOT NULL, slug TEXT UNIQUE, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`. On first initialization, seed the 6 hardcoded sequences (from the current mapping) into this table to guarantee regression parity. |
| **Backend (`main.py`)** | Add `sqlite3` initialization (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) at startup. Implement new endpoints (e.g. `GET /sequencias` to list the catalog directly from DB, `POST /sequencias` to create a new one). For search, implement a new flow that takes a sequence ID (from this catalog), fetches that specific sequence from DB, normalizes nothing on input (as requested), runs contiguous match (`cifra[i : i + len(target)] == target`) against `Musica.cifra`, applies `apply_filtro()` by genre, and paginates exactly like the current sequence path. Replace usage of the old hardcoded `main.sequencias` for this new feature (use the new endpoints/flow). All responses must remain `json.dumps(...)`. |
| **Matching** | Strictly contiguous, in order, anywhere in the song. No `set()`, no subsequence with gaps. Fetch target from DB per request (no caching of the catalog in memory). |
| **Frontend (`static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js`, `static/templates/sequencia.html`)** | Fetch catalog from `GET /sequencias` (DB-backed). Rework the creation UI to be inspired by `#/poracordes`: render all chord groups (same hex set as `AcordesController`), allow clicking hexes to build an ordered `meusAcordes` array for the sequence (append in click order, remove on click like `addAcorde`), display the built sequence, and `POST` it to `POST /sequencias`. On conflict (duplicate ordered sequence), the UI must surface the rejection. Selection of a sequence from the catalog must trigger the new search flow. |
| **Infra** | Docker must use a volume to persist `data/sequencias.db` (e.g. `-v ciframe-data:/app/data` or bind mount). The single `Dockerfile` and local-only constraint from `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` remain unchanged. No external services added. | 

### Trade-offs

| Pros | Benefits |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Meets all explicit changes** | No in-memory sequence cache, DB fetched on demand; catalog comes straight from DB to frontend; `/porsequencia` mirrors `#/poracordes` for creation. |
| **Correct semantics** | Enforces contiguous match exactly as specified. |
| **Safe for regression** | Seed 6 originals into DB and verify against the contiguous test (must produce identical results). |
| **Simple concurrency** | Anonymous, open catalog. Conflicts rejected at DB level (e.g. UNIQUE on the ordered representation). |
| **Fits local-only + SQLite** | Single file on volume, stdlib only, compatible with `Dockerfile`. |

| Cons | Risks |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Per-request DB reads** | Fetching catalog/list by ID from SQLite on each search/list is cheap for a small catalog, but must be efficient (prepared statements). |
| **No precomputation** | Every search scans up to ~67k songs with contiguous check (with genre filter). Acceptable per requirement to run in real-time. |
| **UX on errors** | Must clearly show conflict rejection on `POST /sequencias`. |
| **Migration of source of truth** | Must fully cut over from hardcoded `main.sequencias` for this feature to avoid mixed behavior. |

### Validation

| Check | Method |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Regression** | Run contiguous test for all 6 original DB-seeded sequences - all must return the same sets (missing = 0). |
| **Matching rule** | Verify gaps invalidate (contiguous only). Test examples like `Victor e Leo - Fotos` only matches if the exact contiguous block exists. |
| **Persistence** | Create custom sequence via POST, `docker restart` (or stop/start with volume mounted), `GET /sequencias` still returns it. |
| **API contract** | New endpoint family returns `json.dumps` strings, CORS unchanged. Pagination identical to current sequence search. |
| **Frontend parity** | `/porsequencia` loads catalog from GET, creation UI mirrors `/poracordes` click-to-build, POST works anonymously. |
| **Conflicts** | Attempt to POST duplicate ordered sequence -> rejected (no creation). |

### Open Questions
- **New endpoint shape**: Exact paths (e.g. `GET /sequencias`, `POST /sequencias`, and `GET /similares/porsequencia?id=...` or another new search endpoint) - must be a new endpoint family as requested. Need to confirm routing doesn't conflict with existing `/similares?sequencia=...` (will be replaced by the new flow for this feature).
- **ID format**: Use integer primary key from DB for lookup. 
- **Storage of ordered sequence**: Serialize as `acordes_json` (array in click order). Comparison for conflicts must use this exact ordered representation (no normalization).
- **Volume mounting**: Document exact `docker run` example with volume (bind or named) to satisfy "utilizaremos um volume para garantir a persistencia".


## Proposal 2 — Hybrid DB + Isolated Search Module (Stricter Separation)
*More explicit architectural separation, same runtime matching, but isolates the new feature into its own module/endpoints with stricter boundaries.*

### Overview
Same as Proposal 1 (SQLite on volume, DB-only catalog, no in-memory cache, contiguous runtime matching, `#/poracordes`-inspired UI), but extract sequence catalog and matching into a dedicated module (e.g. `sequencias.py`) and expose only the new endpoint family. This makes the cut-over from the old hardcoded mechanism explicit and easier to reason about, with zero coupling to the legacy `main.sequencias` dict beyond seeding. 

### Key Changes

| Component | Changes |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Structure** | New `sequencias.py` for DB access, validation (conflict detection), and contiguous matching. `main.py` imports and wires new routes only. |
| **Persistence/Infra** | Identical to P1 (SQLite on mounted volume, seeded 6 originals). |
| **Endpoints** | Dedicated new family (e.g. `GET /api/sequencias`, `POST /api/sequencias`, `GET /api/sequencias/<id>/musicas` for search) to fully decouple from legacy `?sequencia=` path. Enforce POST+GET as requested. |
| **Matching** | Same contiguous logic, fetched from DB per request. Pagination identical. |
| **Frontend** | Same UX changes as P1, calling the new endpoint family. |

### Trade-offs

| Pros | Benefits |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Cleaner cut-over** | Forces removal of hardcoded dependencies, reduces risk of accidentally reusing old paths. |
| **Testability** | Matching logic isolated and easier to unit test. |
| **Future-proof** | Clear boundary for this feature. |

| Cons | Risks |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Slightly more boilerplate** | New module and potentially new route structure. |
| **API shape deviation** | If we don't keep search semantics identical in structure, need to ensure frontend maps correctly to "same results expected". |
| **More files touched** | Marginally larger diff, but still within scope. |

### Validation

Same as Proposal 1, with additional checks for module isolation and that no legacy code path is used for the new feature.

### Open Questions
- **Route naming**: Should the search be nested under sequences or a new dedicated route? Must still return results in the same format as expected (compatible with existing rendering expectations). 


## Recommendation

**Go with Proposal 1 (New `/sequencias` endpoint family + runtime contiguous matching, DB-on-demand)**.

- **Exactly matches the user's changes**: No in-memory sequence cache (DB fetched directly), creation UI inspired by `#/poracordes` (click hexes to build ordered sequence), SQLite on volume, no normalization, replace with new feature for matching, same pagination, real-time, conflicts block creation, implemented via new endpoint family (POST+GET).
- **Correct semantics**: Contiguous match on `Musica.cifra` enforces "appear complete and exactly in order anywhere" as confirmed by our tests.
- **Minimal, safe cut-over**: Seed 6 originals into DB to guarantee identical results. Keep songs/genres in CSV untouched. Respects `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (single Dockerfile, local-only, no external services).
- **Pragmatic for local-only**: Runtime scan is acceptable and avoids the complexity of denormalized match tables.

**Implementation notes for P1:**
1. **DB setup**: Initialize SQLite in `data/` (mounted volume). `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sequencias(...)`. Seed from existing 6-sequence mapping on first run.
2. **Endpoints**: Add `GET /sequencias` and `POST /sequencias` (new family). Implement search via the new flow (fetch sequence by ID from DB, contiguous match, apply genre filter, paginate). 
3. **Matching**: `for i in range(len(cifra)-len(t)+1): if cifra[i:i+len(t)] == t: return True` with target from DB, no normalization.
4. **Frontend**: Rewrite `sequencia.js/html` to fetch from `GET /sequencias`, use `AcordesController`-style chord groups for selection to build ordered array, POST to `POST /sequencias`, handle conflict rejection.
5. **Infra**: Update run instructions to use a volume (e.g. `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v $(pwd)/data:/app/data ciframe`) to guarantee persistence.

No front muda que teremos uma nova tela acessivel a partir de `#porsequencia`, `#cadastra-seqfamosa` com um "form" preenchido com a mesma UI que existe para a escolha dos acorde em `#poracorde` e apos a inserção essa sequence o usuário eh redirecionado para a tela `#porsequencia`ja atualiza com musicas filtradas pela nova sequencia cadastrada, na mesma tela com sequencias na esquerda e musicas na diretia, como ja aconetce hoej.

## Solution Proposals

**Context:**
- Request: Implement a feature allowing any visitor to register a new chord sequence and search for songs by it, exactly like the 6 pre-existing famous sequences. The sequence catalog must be persisted in a database (SQLite), survive container restarts via a volume, and be fetched directly from the DB (no in-memory catalog). A new screen `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` must exist, accessible from `#/porsequencia`. This new screen must use the exact same chord selection UI as `#/poracordes` to build an ordered sequence (clicking the chord hexes to append to the sequence). After successfully creating the sequence via POST, the user must be redirected to `#/porsequencia` with that newly created sequence already selected, causing the results to be filtered by it. The `#/porsequencia` screen must keep the same layout as today (sequences on the left, results on the right) but the list of sequences must come from the backend (DB). Only the sequence catalog moves to the DB - songs and genres must remain in the CSV loaded in memory as today. Matching must be contiguous: the sequence must appear complete and exactly in order anywhere in `Musica.cifra`. Conflicts must prevent creation. The feature must be implemented through a new endpoint family (POST and GET). The 6 original sequences must continue producing the same results.
- Research Source: `research/codebase-overview.md` (bootstrap, `/similares` routing, `Musica.cifra` vs `Musica.acordes`, `seqs_famosas` path, frontend templates), `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md` (local-only Docker, single container, no external services), `docs/features/sequencias-customizadas/00-enunciado.md` (requirements), `main.py:40-45,170-223,230-263`, `musica.py:1-25`, `static/templates/sequencia.html`, `static/templates/acordes.html`, `static/assets/js/controllers/acordes.js`, `static/assets/js/controllers/sequencia.js`


## Proposal 1 — New Endpoint Family + Dedicated Cadastro Route (DB-On-Demand)
*Most aligned with the requested UX. Keeps the existing `#/porsequencia` layout intact whilst adding a new cadastro flow.* 

### Overview
Introduce a new endpoint family for the sequence catalog (`GET /sequencias`, `POST /sequencias`). Persist only the catalog to SQLite on a mounted volume, seeding the 6 original sequences on first boot. Add a new route/view `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` that mirrors the chord selection from `#/poracordes` to build an ordered sequence and POST it. On success, redirect to `#/porsequencia` with the newly created sequence pre-selected so results are fetched and rendered on the right panel, exactly like the current behavior. Searching will fetch the target sequence directly from the DB at match time and run a contiguous scan against `Musica.cifra`. 


### Key Changes

| Component | Changes |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Persistence (`data/`)** | Create `data/sequencias.db` on a mounted volume. Table `sequencias(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, nome TEXT, acordes_json TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`. Add a UNIQUE constraint on the ordered representation (e.g. on `acordes_json` or a normalized form of the ordered list) to enforce conflict prevention. Seed the 6 originals on first initialization. |
| **Backend (`main.py`)** | Add `sqlite3` init at boot (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + seed). New endpoint family: `GET /sequencias` (list catalog directly from DB, no in-memory cache) and `POST /sequencias` (validate ordered list, reject conflicts with 409/appropriate response, insert into DB). Add a new search flow for the new catalog (fetch sequence by ID from DB, run contiguous match `cifra[i : i+len(target)] == target` against `Musica.cifra`, apply `apply_filtro()` by genre, paginate exactly like today). Keep all responses as `json.dumps(...)`. Do not add normalization to user input. |
| **Routing (AngularJS)** | Add a new route for `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` in `app.js` pointing to a new controller/template. Add navigation from `#/porsequencia` to `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` (e.g. a "Cadastrar nova sequência" button/link). On successful POST, redirect to `#/porsequencia` passing the new sequence's identifier (e.g. via query params or state) so that it is auto-selected. |
| **Frontend - Cadastro (`#/cadastra-seqfamosa`)** | New template/controller inspired by `static/templates/acordes.html` and `static/assets/js/controllers/acordes.js`. Reuse the same chord groupings and hex rendering (`df-hex` directive), build an ordered array `sequenciaAcordes` on click (append on click, remove on click, preserving order), display the built sequence, and POST to `POST /sequencias`. Keep the same visual language as `#/poracordes`. |
| **Frontend - Por Sequencia (`#/porsequencia`)** | Update `sequencia.js/html` to fetch the catalog from `GET /sequencias` (DB-backed, no hardcoded JS list). Keep left panel for sequences and right panel for results, identical layout to today. When arriving from cadastro with a pre-selected sequence, trigger the search automatically to render results on the right panel. |
| **Infra** | Use a mounted volume for persistence (e.g. `-v $(pwd)/data:/app/data` or named volume). Remain within the single `Dockerfile` and local-only constraints of `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md`. No external services. | 

### Trade-offs

| Pros | Cons |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Perfectly matches UX** | New route, controller and template add files but are isolated. |
| **DB is source of truth** | No in-memory cache, fetched directly from DB as requested. |
| **Correct matching** | Contiguous, in order, anywhere in `Musica.cifra`. No normalization. |
| **Seamless flow** | Redirect back to `#/porsequencia` with auto-selection creates a smooth experience. |
| **Regression safe** | Seed 6 originals and validate with the contiguous test. |
| **Respects all constraints** | Volume for persistence, new endpoint family, songs/genres untouched, pagination preserved, real-time matching. |

| Cons | Risks |
| :-- | :-- |
| **More frontend work** | Need to replicate `#/poracordes` UI logic and handle route/state passing. |
| **DB reads on demand** | Catalog fetched on read (cheap) and sequence fetched per search; acceptable for local-only. |
| **State transfer** | Need to ensure the new sequence ID is passed correctly on redirect (query param or shared service). |
| **Conflict UX** | Must clearly display rejection on POST (duplicate ordered sequence). | 

### Validation

| Check | Method |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Regression** | Run contiguous test against all 6 DB-seeded sequences - must produce identical results to today. |
| **Cadastro flow** | Create a new sequence via `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` using the chord UI, POST succeeds, redirect to `#/porsequencia`, new sequence is selected and results render on right panel. |
| **Persistence** | Create sequence, restart container with volume mounted, sequence still appears in `GET /sequencias` and works in `#/porsequencia`. |
| **Matching rule** | Verify only contiguous matches work. Test a case where chords are split by others (must not match). |
| **Conflicts** | Attempt to create an identical ordered sequence -> rejected, no duplicate created. |
| **API contract** | New endpoints return `json.dumps` strings, CORS unchanged, pagination identical. |

### Open Questions
- **Route naming**: Confirm exact route string `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` (as requested). 
- **State passing**: Use `$location.search()` or a shared AngularJS service to pass the newly created sequence ID to `#/porsequencia` for auto-selection.
- **Conflict response**: Decide on HTTP status/body for duplicate (e.g. 409) and how the UI surfaces it.
- **Sequence identifier**: Use the integer DB ID for lookup in the search flow to match the "fetch from DB at match time" requirement.


## Proposal 2 — Modal Cadastro from `#/porsequencia` (Same Flow, Different Entry Point)
*Same backend/logic as Proposal 1, but instead of a new full page, use a modal overlay on `#/porsequencia` for cadastro. The UX differs from the explicit new route requested.*

### Overview
Keep all backend changes identical (SQLite on volume, DB-on-demand catalog, new endpoint family, contiguous matching). On `#/porsequencia`, add a "Cadastrar nova sequência" button that opens a modal inspired by `#/poracordes` chord selection to build and POST the sequence. On success, close modal, refresh catalog from `GET /sequencias`, auto-select the newly created sequence, and filter results on the right panel. 

### Key Changes
| Component | Changes |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Backend/Infra** | Identical to Proposal 1. |
| **Frontend** | Modal on `sequencia.html` using the same chord groups/UI as `#/poracordes`. No new route/controller necessarily. Catalog refresh after creation. |

### Trade-offs
| Pros | Cons |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Fewer routes** | Simpler routing changes. |
| **Stays in same context** | User never leaves `#/porsequencia`. | 
| **Does not match the explicit requirement** | The request explicitly states: *"teremos uma nova tela acessivel a partir de `#porsequencia`, `#cadastra-seqfamosa`"*. A modal is not a new screen/route. |

### Recommendation

**Reject Proposal 2 for this task.** The requirement is explicit about a new screen `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` accessible from `#/porsequencia`. Proposal 1 fulfills this exactly. 

## Recommendation (Final)

**Go with Proposal 1 — New `/sequencias` endpoint family + `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` route + runtime contiguous matching.**

This directly implements every requested change:

- **Persistence**: SQLite in `data/` on a mounted volume. Catalog fetched directly from DB (no in-memory cache). Seeded with the 6 originals for regression parity.
- **Endpoints**: New endpoint family `GET /sequencias` and `POST /sequencias`. Conflicts block creation (UNIQUE on ordered representation). No normalization of input.
- **Matching**: Fetch sequence by ID from DB at match time, contiguous scan on `Musica.cifra` (`i : i+len == target`), apply genre filter, same pagination, real-time. Only this new feature is used for matching going forward.
- **Frontend**: New screen `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` inspired by `#/poracordes` (all chord hexes, click to build ordered sequence), accessible from `#/porsequencia`. After POST success, redirect to `#/porsequencia` with the new sequence auto-selected so results update on the right panel, keeping the exact left/right layout as today. `#/porsequencia` now loads sequences from `GET /sequencias`.
- **Constraints**: Songs/genres remain in CSV in memory. Single `Dockerfile`, local-only, no external services. All responses `json.dumps(...)`. 

**Implementation priorities:**
1. **DB schema + seed**: Create SQLite on volume, seed 6 originals, enforce conflict constraint.
2. **Backend**: Implement `GET /sequencias`, `POST /sequencias`, and the new contiguous match flow for the new catalog. Wire routes.
3. **Frontend routing**: Add `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` route, add link from `#/porsequencia` to it.
4. **Cadastro UI**: Replicate `#/poracordes` chord selection to build ordered sequence and POST, handle conflicts, redirect with selected ID.
5. **Porsequencia UI**: Fetch catalog from DB, support auto-selection on arrival, keep existing layout and pagination.
6. **Validation**: Regression test against 6 originals, persistence test with volume, conflict test, contiguous-match test.

## Solution Proposals

**Context:**
- Request: Implement a feature allowing any visitor to register a new chord sequence and search for songs by it, exactly like the 6 pre-existing famous sequences. The sequence catalog must be persisted in a database (SQLite), survive container restarts via a volume, and be fetched directly from the DB (no in-memory catalog). A new screen `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` must exist, accessible from `#/porsequencia`. This new screen must use the exact same chord selection UI as `#/poracordes` to build an ordered sequence (clicking the chord hexes to append to the sequence). After successfully creating the sequence via POST, the user must be redirected to `#/porsequencia` with that newly created sequence already selected, causing the results to be filtered by it. The `#/porsequencia` screen must keep the same layout as today (sequences on the left, results on the right) but the list of sequences must come from the backend (DB). Only the sequence catalog moves to the DB - songs and genres must remain in the CSV loaded in memory as today. Matching must be contiguous: the sequence must appear complete and exactly in order anywhere in `Musica.cifra`. Conflicts must prevent creation. The feature must be implemented through a new endpoint family (POST and GET). The 6 original sequences must continue producing the same results.

## Proposal 1 — Minimal SQLite Schema + `#/cadastra-seqfamousa` Route (DB-On-Demand)
*Most aligned with the feedback. Minimal schema, seed on table creation, no in-memory catalog.*

### Overview

Create a new endpoint family (`GET /sequencias`, `POST /sequencias`) backed by SQLite. The schema will be as minimal as possible, with the 6 existing sequences inserted directly at table creation time using the exact same ordered lists currently hardcoded in the backend. The catalog is never kept in memory: both `#/porsequencia` and the match flow fetch it directly from the DB. A new route `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` will mirror `#/poracordes` to build an ordered sequence by clicking the hexes, POST it to the new endpoint, and redirect back to `#/porsequencia` with it pre-selected to show results on the right panel.

### Key Changes

| Component | Changes |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Persistence (`data/`)** | Create `data/sequencias.db` on a **mounted volume**. Table: `sequencias(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, acordes_json TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)`. Right after `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, insert the 6 original sequences from `main.sequencias`/the existing hardcoded mapping using `INSERT OR IGNORE` (preferably with explicit IDs to avoid any ambiguity). No `nome`, no `created_at`. |
| **Backend (`main.py`)** | Add `sqlite3` initialization at startup. Implement `GET /sequencias` returning all rows from the DB (parsed from `acordes_json` to the array form the frontend expects). Implement `POST /sequencias` receiving an ordered list of chords (in click order). Serialize to JSON and attempt `INSERT`. Enforce conflict via `UNIQUE(acordes_json)` -> return an error on duplicate and prevent creation. For the search/match flow used by this feature, fetch the target sequence by its `id` directly from the DB at request time and run a **contiguous** match against `Musica.cifra` (`cifra[i : i+len(target)] == target`). Apply `apply_filtro()` by genre and keep the same pagination as today. All responses must remain `json.dumps(...)`. No input normalization. |
| **Routing (AngularJS)** | Add route `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` in `app.js` pointing to a new controller/template. Add a link/button from `#/porsequencia` to `#/cadastra-seqfamosa`. On successful POST, redirect to `#/porsequencia` passing the newly created sequence's `id` (e.g. via `$location.path('/porsequencia').search({sequencia: id})`) so it gets auto-selected. |
| **Frontend - Cadastro (`#/cadastra-seqfamosa`)** | New template and controller inspired by `#/poracordes`. Reuse the same chord groupings, colors and `df-hex` directive. Maintain an ordered array `sequencia` appending on click and removing on click (preserving order), mirroring `AcordesController.addAcorde` behavior. Display the built sequence clearly. On submit, `POST` the array to `/sequencias`. On conflict, show rejection. On success, redirect to `#/porsequencia` with that sequence selected. |
| **Frontend - Por Sequencia (`#/porsequencia`)** | Update `sequencia.js` and `sequencia.html` to load the catalog from `GET /sequencias` (no hardcoded list). Keep the exact left/right layout as today. On load, if a `sequencia` id comes via query params (from cadastro redirect), auto-select it and trigger the search to render results on the right panel. |
| **Infra** | Use a mounted volume for persistence (e.g. `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v $(pwd)/data:/app/data ciframe`). Keep single `Dockerfile` and local-only as per `docs/adr/0001-local-only-docker-deploy.md`. No external services. | 

### Trade-offs

| Pros | Cons |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Truly minimal schema** | Only `id` and `acordes_json` needed. No unused fields. |
| **Seeded at table creation** | The 6 originals are guaranteed to exist from day one without a separate "migration" step. Easier to enforce regression parity. |
| **No in-memory catalog** | Directly fetches from DB, matches the requested "não precisamo manter as sequencias em memória". |
| **Exactly matches UX** | New dedicated screen, same `#/poracordes` interaction, redirect back to `#/porsequencia` with auto-selection and results on the right. |
| **Strict semantics** | Contiguous match, no normalization, conflicts block creation, new endpoint family. |
| **Simple persistence** | SQLite on volume is enough and fits all constraints. | 

| Cons | Risks |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Frontend must derive display** | Since there's no `nome`, the UI must display the sequence by joining `acordes_json` (same visual as today). |
| **ID stability** | If we want to be extra safe for parity, seed with fixed IDs for the 6 originals. |
| **Catalog fetches on demand** | `GET /sequencias` will be called by `#/porsequencia`; cheap enough for local-only use. |

### Validation

| Check | Method |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Regression** | Seed the 6 originals into DB and run the contiguous test against them. Must produce identical result sets to current behavior. |
| **Cadastro flow** | From `#/porsequencia` -> `#/cadastra-seqfamosa`, build ordered sequence by clicking hexes (same as `#/poracordes`), POST to `/sequencias`, get redirected to `#/porsequencia` with that sequence selected and results rendered on right panel. |
| **Persistence** | Create a new sequence, `docker stop`/`docker rm` and run with the same volume mounted, `GET /sequencias` returns it and `#/porsequencia` can search by it. |
| **Conflicts** | POST the exact same ordered sequence again -> rejected, DB remains unchanged. |
| **Matching rule** | Test contiguous only (chords with gaps must not match). Verify fetch-by-id from DB at match time. |
| **Contract** | Endpoints use `json.dumps(...)`, pagination unchanged, songs/genres still from CSV in memory. |

### Open Questions
- **Seed IDs**: Assign fixed IDs to the 6 originals at insert time to keep them predictable, or just rely on insertion order. Either is fine as long as results are identical.
- **Response shape**: `GET /sequencias` should return something like `[{ "id": 1, "acordes": ["C","G","Am","F"] }, ...]` parsed from `acordes_json` to be easy for AngularJS to render.
- **POST body**: Accept `{"acordes": ["C","G","Am","F"]}` (array in click order). Reject empty arrays.


## Proposal 2 — Reuse `/similares` with a New DB-Backed Resolver (Less Route Split)
*Technically possible, but less aligned with "new endpoint family (POST and GET)".*

### Overview
Keep a similar shape to existing search but resolve the sequence entirely from DB by id via the new endpoints. Still add `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` as a new screen and redirect flow. Backend would add `GET /sequencias` and `POST /sequencias` but try to keep search under `/similares` by extending it to look up from SQLite. 

### Trade-offs

| Pros | Cons |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Fewer new routes** | Less frontend route wiring. | 
| **Explicitly requested** | The requirement says: *"A feat precisa ser implementada em um novo endpoint, tendo em vista que ele será utilizado com POST e GET."* Extending `/similares` blurs the "new endpoint family" and goes against that instruction. |

**Not recommended.** Stick to Proposal 1 with a dedicated `GET /sequencias` and `POST /sequencias`.

## Recommendation

**Go with Proposal 1.**

- **Schema**: `sequencias(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, acordes_json TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)`. No `nome`, no `timestamp`. 
- **Seed on init**: After `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, insert the 6 sequences that exist today in the backend (with their exact ordered chord lists) using `INSERT OR IGNORE`. 
- **Persistence**: SQLite file in `data/` on a mounted volume.
- **Endpoints**: New endpoint family `GET /sequencias` and `POST /sequencias`. Conflicts blocked by `UNIQUE`. 
- **Matching**: Fetch sequence by id from DB at match time, contiguous scan on `Musica.cifra`, same genre filter + pagination, real-time. 
- **Frontend**: New `#/cadastra-seqfamosa` screen mirroring `#/poracordes` (click hexes to build ordered sequence), accessible from `#/porsequencia`. On POST success redirect to `#/porsequencia` with the new sequence auto-selected so results appear on the right panel. `#/porsequencia` reads catalog from `GET /sequencias`. 
- **Constraints**: Songs/genres remain in CSV in memory. Single Dockerfile, local-only, no external services, `json.dumps` responses, no input normalization.
